We are an Australian-Thai team that has organised tours on Koh Samui and Koh Phangan since 2006, licensed by the Tourism Authority of Thailand under licence 43/01467. We sell boat trips from Samui to Ang Thong Marine Park, Pig Island, Koh Tao and the Koh Phangan parties, plus private boats, and we write the island guides on this site. Prices are charged in THB, you pay by card through a secure checkout, and day trips are fully refundable when you cancel 48 hours or more before departure.

Our story since 2006

The business started in 2006 with day trips from the islands of the Samui archipelago and has grown into a small network of island sites run by one team. Over 20 years we have watched the Gulf of Thailand change: new piers, faster boats, the Samui airport handling more flights, and stricter national park rules at Ang Thong. What hasn't changed is the job: get guests to the islands and back safely, on time, at a fair price, and tell them the truth about the weather.

This site is the Koh Samui member of that network. It follows the same booking system, the same cancellation policy and the same standards as kohphangan.com, which our team has run for years, but every guide here is written for Samui: its piers, its roads, its seasons and the trips that leave from it.

How we check facts

Island information goes out of date fast. Ferry prices change, visa rules changed on 15 September 2026, and park fees move. Our rules:

  • We check facts against primary sources: Thai government pages, the national park authority, operators' own timetables and our own crews.
  • We review prices and dates on money pages every month and event dates every week.
  • Every page shows an "Updated" date, and fact boxes show when they were last verified.
  • Anything we can't confirm stays off the page until we can.
  • No paid placements, no sponsored rankings and no fabricated reviews.

The full process is on our editorial policy page.

Safety first

We cancel or reschedule when the sea isn't safe, even on a sunny morning. The captain's call is final, and you then choose a full refund or a new date. Life jackets, including children's sizes, are on every boat and must be worn by children on board. The north-east monsoon makes October to December the roughest months on the east coast, which is why we publish live sea conditions and move guests to sheltered south-west trips from Thong Krut when the east side is closed. Our safety guide covers rip currents, box jellyfish and road risks.

Responsible tourism

  • No elephant riding. We don't sell or recommend riding or animal shows. See our elephant sanctuary guide for what to look for in an ethical visit.
  • The Pig Island pigs. We ask guests not to chase or lift the pigs and never to feed them junk food or alcohol.
  • Reefs. Don't stand on or touch coral, and don't feed fish. Thailand's national park authority bans sunscreens with coral-harming chemicals such as oxybenzone in marine national parks, so pack a reef-safe one for Ang Thong.
  • Rubbish. Take everything back to the boat. Koh Nang Yuan bans plastic bottles on the island.

Corrections and contact
